newsitem.title: INDIA: India SBI to raise SBICI capital to 1.0 bln rupees.
newsitem.headline: India SBI to raise SBICI capital to 1.0 bln rupees.

text.p: The State Bank of India (SBI) said it planned to raise the paid up capital of its subsidiary SBI Commercial & International (SBICI) to 1.0 billion rupees.
"We will inject another 500 million rupees before the year-end," SBI chairman P.G. Kakodkar told Reuters on Monday.
SBICI is currently capitalised at 500 million rupees.

"We want it (SBICI) to face the competition from the agile, small, private banks," he said, referring to nine new private banks established after the government allowed private sector banks as part of the economic reforms launched in 1991.
Kakodkar said SBI was facing competition from these private banks in cities.

"They are small, more agile and have better technology," he said. "They have no baggage of NPAs (non-performing assets)," he said, listing the advantages private banks had over SBI, a state-run bank with a long history.
SBICI was established in January 1994 after SBI took over the Bombay branch of the erstwhile Bank of Credit and Commerce International. SBICI is a wholly-owned subsidiary of SBI.
SBI is India's largest commercial bank.
